items.title: High earners face more social security contributions in 2027
items.body: In 2027, Spain will raise social security contributions for high salaries and companies for the third consecutive year. The MEI rate rises from 0.9% in 2026 to 1%, with employers paying 0.83% and workers 0.17%. A higher maximum contribution base and solidarity quota add to the bill, while maximum pensions revalue more slowly, so high earners pay more without equivalent future pension benefits.

items.title: EU: return Ceuta migrants; hundreds back at beach camp
items.body: The European Commission said Spain has a duty to protect unaccompanied migrant minors who crossed into Ceuta and expects all irregular entrants to be returned to Morocco. Hours later, Ceuta suspended cleanup at El Trampolín beach after around 500 migrants returned, following relocation of over 1,200 people to two new shelters. The back-and-forth keeps border migration pressure high.

items.title: EU sets new €10,000 cash payment limit from 2027
items.body: From July 10, 2027, an EU regulation caps cash payments at €10,000 for single or related transactions in goods and services. The rule applies to financial entities, auditors, tax advisors, notaries, lawyers, and certain goods traders; football clubs and agents are included from July 10, 2029. Large cash purchases in Spain will require bank transfers instead.

items.title: Analyst: Banning home purchases for investment is unconstitutional
items.body: Real estate analyst Sergio Gutiérrez says a Catalan proposal to restrict home purchases in stressed areas to primary residence or habitual rental violates constitutional principles. Inherited properties would need to be occupied or rented within 12 months. The Consell de Garanties Estatutàries found potential violations of property, inheritance, business freedom, and legal security.

items.title: Expert: Rent increases above legal limits are illegal, don't accept
items.body: Real estate expert Alberto Sánchez advises tenants that landlords cannot raise rent whenever they want and must follow legal limits. Tenants should know their rights to defend against illegal increases. The warning comes as many renters face pressure to pay above legally allowed amounts.

items.title: Hacienda can detect your rental; declare home even without deduction
items.body: Taxpayers must correctly identify their habitual residence in the income tax return, even if not claiming rental deductions, because Hacienda can cross-check data. Renters under 38 in Madrid can deduct up to €1,200, for example. Failure to provide accurate information may trigger checks.

items.title: Fuel prices rise for seventh week after VAT reduction ends
items.body: Fuel prices have increased for seven consecutive weeks since the reduced VAT ended in early July. Diesel rose 0.38% this week to €1.828 per liter, while gasoline rose 0.17% to €1.705. Diesel is up 21.5% and gasoline 18.5% since the VAT break ended. August is expected to see 54.5 million long-distance trips.

items.title: 23.4% of low-educated workers get temporary contracts
items.body: A study shows 23.4% of workers with low education start on temporary contracts, compared with 14% of graduates. Unemployment is 21.8% for those with primary education or less, 12% for secondary, and 6.2% for higher education. The data, based on EPA figures from 2005 to Q2 2026, links lower education to less stable jobs.

items.title: Raising retirement age increases premature mortality, doesn't cut pension costs
items.body: A Fedea study of 179,000 retirees found 282 additional deaths among people aged 60 to 67 due to longer working life, with stronger effects in arduous professions such as miners, railway workers, and firefighters. The pension bill does not decrease despite later retirement.

items.title: Wildfires burn 262,030 hectares in Spain; Las Hurdes evacuees return
items.body: Spain has recorded 262,030 hectares burned and 43 large forest fires from January 1 to August 20, 2026, according to provisional MITECO data. In Las Hurdes, residents of three evacuated hamlets can return home while the Pinofranqueado fire has burned 4,800 hectares and remains at level 2. AEMET forecasts a temperature drop and rain in the north and northeast this weekend.

items.title: Santander completes Webster Bank purchase, becomes top-10 US retail bank
items.body: Banco Santander closed the acquisition of Webster Bank for about €10.5 billion, becoming one of the ten largest retail banks in the United States. The deal involved a capital increase of about €3.5 billion, with 65% paid in cash and 35% in new shares. US authorities and the ECB approved the transaction.

items.title: Tax agency has 35 open investigations into fuel fraud
items.body: Spain's Tax Agency is investigating 35 cases of possible VAT fraud in the hydrocarbon sector, following the Aldama case involving €180 million in fraud. Five of the top ten tax debtors are fuel companies owing about €900 million, including Bio Zenite Energy (€232.9 million), Metaway Combustibles (€195.6 million), and Vertix Petroleum (€194.7 million).
